claims.text: High-pressure torsion can improve the hardness of high-entropy alloys.
High-pressure torsion can improve the strength of high-entropy alloys.
High-pressure torsion can produce these improvements without sacrificing useful mechanical performance.
High-pressure torsion produces grain refinement in high-entropy alloys.
High-pressure torsion introduces lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Grain refinement acts as a barrier to dislocation movement.
Lattice distortion or related solid-solution effects can increase strength in high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion or related solid-solution effects can increase hardness in high-entropy alloys.
Room-temperature HPT at 5 GPa for five turns is sufficient to produce the proposed improvement.
HPT will increase Vickers hardness by at least 20% relative to an untreated baseline.
HPT will increase yield strength by at least 15% relative to an untreated baseline.
The improvement will be greatest in alloys that develop a high degree of lattice distortion and grain refinement during HPT.
A hardness or strength increase below 10% is defined as a falsifying result.
A tensile-ductility reduction greater than 20% is defined as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The predicted minimum improvements are 20% in hardness and 15% in yield strength, but the experiment only falsifies improvements below 10%. Results between 10% and the respective predicted thresholds would fail the prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.
